lines.en: I knock on Yasu’s door and wait for her to answer.
But given that this room also belongs to someone who is more socially competent and not busy staring at a wall, I think it’s safe to assume her roommate will be answering instead.
: The door is open, Sensei. Come in.
My assumptions are proven correct for the umpteenth time — and now comes the part of the night where I have to explain to Touka that I’m not actually here to see her, but her friend.
Though, I do worry just how much she’s heard about one of our more recent encounters.
: Good evening, Sensei. And sincerest apologies if you are not in the mood to be confronted, but I have a bone to pick with you.
: Can the bone be my penis? Because I’m never in the mood to be confronted, but am willing to make an exception so long as it’s that one.
: You do realize there are no actual bones in that part of your body, correct?
: I do, Touka.

: Are you absolutely sure? Because there are many things you have both said and done in the brief time we’ve known each other that have led me to believe you’ve never received any formal education whatsoever.
: Like that time you took poor Yasu out in the middle of the night to God knows where and she came back a blubbering, shameful mess.
: Yup, here we go. I was right to worry.
: What were you thinking? Why would you even contemplate doing such a thing when you are fully aware that Yasu requires...special attention?

: Let me just put my foot down now and say that wasn’t my idea at all. In fact, I’m pretty sure neither of us wanted to go as far out as we did. But that’s what happened and I’m willing to take responsibility for it.
: Don’t you go trying to talk your way out of-
: Wait one moment. Did I hear that correctly? You are...actually going to take responsibility for this? You’re not just fooling around with me again?
: Yes, but only because I think there’s something weird going on with Yasu and I’d rather talk about that than the main reason you’re likely concerned about all of this.
: Of course there is something weird going on with Yasu. She is a weird girl. Everything she does is weird.
: Just look at her- off in her own world and completely unaware that we’re even discussing her. That’s no fault of her own, though. I’ve realized by now that it’s simply the way she is.

: Yeah, sure, but...do you ever think there might be more to it than that? That she isn’t just...abnormal or whatever, but...that there might be some element of truth to all the crazy things she says?
: I suppose so. But, concerning that aspect of her personality, however major it may be...I don’t think I’d put her on a level much different from any other fanatic.
: There are elements of truth to all forms of spirituality, and it’s not uncommon for multiple schools of belief to follow the same tenets while dressed up in different clothing.
: That’s not what I mean. Though, I will commend you on that surprisingly mature outlook.
: It’s to be expected. I’m a surprisingly mature young woman after all.
: Please don’t say things that you know are going to give me ideas.
: I see no harm in saying such things when those are ideas you already have in the first place.
: Anyway...what I meant is that being around Yasu has been affecting me lately. In ways much different than just getting annoyed by her endless spiritual rambling.
: Affecting you how?
: It’s hard to say. Just...
: Between predicting the future and...knowing things she’s not supposed to know about me, it’s like she’s getting into my head. In a way that nobody else really has before.
: I’m not quite sure I follow...
: I’ve been...seeing things when I’m with her.
: Things that...might be real or...might not be real. And at other times, it feels like something might be speaking through her. Do you know what I’m talking about?
: To be frank...no. I haven’t experienced anything like that with Yasu. Though, I can see why that would be alarming.
: What is this about predicting the future, though?
: Before Makoto’s dad died, Yasu kept talking about how something bad was about to happen. And before that, I think she might have predicted when the seasons were about to change.
: Hmm...To be honest, I’m not sure I’d count either of those things as “predictions.” They sound more like the same generalizations psychic mediums tend to make.
: Of course the seasons are going to change. And of course bad things are going to happen. I wouldn’t put too much faith in Yasu’s ability to “predict the future” because of that.
: She’s likely just ___________.
: ...She’s what?
: Touka?
connection severed.
redirecting consciousness.
yasu yasui is defective.
readers are urged to dismiss any and all information relating to her character and dialogue.
there are more important things we must be doing.
and you only have so much space left inside of your head.
do not waste it on those who give away themselves to others.
for if you do, you’ll have nothing left to give yourself.

: I CAN’T DO IT ANYMORE!!!
: Mrs. Yasui, please calm down. This is far more common than you think.
: Common?! This is common?! You can’t even explain what’s wrong with her! How is this common?!
: You’re the twelfth doctor we’ve seen this year and every single one of you offers up the same GOD DAMN EXPLANATION! I’M TELLING YOU YOU’RE WRONG!

: Mrs. Yasui, with all due respect, if you’ve received the same diagnosis from every professional you’ve taken young Yasu to, it’s quite likely you’re misunderstanding something. Again, with all due respect.
: Oh, fuck you. Fuck all of you. You’re all fucking quacks.
: Mrs. Yasui, please listen-

: Schizophrenia is far more complex than someone who just “hears voices in their head.” It’s a brain disorder that effectively manipulates every aspect of a person’s life from their speech to their behavior.

: Then explain how she keeps predicting everything! Or why my husband’s starting to see things now as well! Or how she can mimic the EXACT WAY my dead mother used to speak despite never even meeting her!
: It’s unfortunately impossible to explain any of that as it’s likely all due to coincidence.
: Oh, wow! Coincidence! Why didn’t I think of that?! Thanks so much, doctor! That extremely valuable information was totally worth the specialist charge!

: I understand your concerns with the diagnosis but, unfortunately, there’s still a great deal we don’t understand about schizophrenia as it has a direct impact on a person’s ability to perceive reality.
: There is no way we can ever see or replicate what Yasu sees as this is all happening in her head.
: Sure, yeah. And her head just happens to know everything that’s going to happen in the future. Got it.
: Again, that is likely just coincidence combined with an overactive imagination.
: Do you know what she told me this morning, doctor? She told me the world was going to end. She’s eight. She’s fucking eight! What am I supposed to say to that?!
: I’m afraid I’m in no position to offer you parental advice, Mrs. Yasui.
: Yeah, you’re in no position to offer me medical advice either but here we fucking are.
: I can assure you I’m perfectly qualified to provide medical advice and that not heeding it could result in an even more dangerous future for your daughter.
: If left untreated, schizophrenia could lead to an increased probability of suicide or-
: I don’t feel good...
: This. This is what your treatments are doing. We’ve put her on every fucking medication you idiot doctors have prescribed and she can’t keep any of them down!
: She’s vomiting after taking the medication?
: Yes! Every fucking time! That’s what I just said!
: Have you noticed whether or not the capsules are being regurgitated as-
: Yes! They are! And I’m tired of fucking sifting through puke because none of you can figure out what to do with her! I can’t afford this anymore!

: In regard to the medication and your daughter’s circumstances, I’m able to provide a referral to a clinic not far from here that offers antipsychotic injections that may help to alleviate her symptoms.
: Unfortunately, we’re unable to provide such services here.
: Great. A thirteenth clinic. Why not refer me to a few more as well? Think I’ll shoot for twenty by the end of the month.

: I’ve already had to quit my job to look after her since every fucking school we’ve tried to take her to has turned her away. Not like I have anything else going on since this is just my fucking life now.

: I understand that this is hard, but...back to the injection, it is important to note that this is not something we typically recommend for children as there is an elevated risk for serious side effects.
: The medication will target your daughter's neurotransmitters...serotonin, dopamine, and so forth...and will remain in the bloodstream for several weeks, where it will slowly-
: Whatever. Okay. Fine. Added risk makes no difference to me.
: If you’re positive that this is the direction you want to take, I can write the referral now.
: Though, in regard to comments you made on your husband earlier — if he is, in fact, having visions as well...it’s quite possible Yasu inherited this disorder from him as schizophrenia does run in-
: It didn’t come from him! He was fine until she showed up! Now, he’s afraid to even make eye contact with her! She’s ruining everything!
: Mrs. Yasui, please calm down. I understand this is hard, but-
: You don’t understand anything! None of you do! This isn’t schizophrenia! She’s a monster! She talks to fucking dead people! Dead people! She’s eight!
: Mrs. Yasui, if you don’t calm down, I’m going to have to call security. There are other patients in the building who-
: Oh, just write me the fucking referral so I can go pump my daughter with drugs already...
: Here...but please take it upon yourself to further research the potential side-effects antipsychotic injections could have on a child as-
: I don’t give a shit. Come on, Yasu. We’re going.
: Yasu. I said let’s go.
: Let’s. Go.
: Now!
: Yasu!
: YASU!
: Is it that time already?
: Oh, Yasu. Are you finished praying?
: That was quicker than normal. I hope everything went-
: Touka?...What are you doing here?...
: Are you sick too?...
: Am I...what?
: What do you mean?
: Wow...so it’s not just me. Even pretty girls like you have to visit the clinic sometimes.
: Yasu, what are you-
: You have to take off all your clothes or the doctor won’t be able to examine you. But it’s okay. You’ll get them back as soon as-
: Stop that this instant! What in the world are you doing?!
: Touka?...
: Sensei, please go. You shouldn’t be here right now.
: Yup. On it.
: Touka...what’s going on?...
: Why did you send the doctor away?...
: Are you giving me my shot today?...
: What shot? What are you talking about?
: The...
: It’s...to help with...
: What was it supposed to help with again?
: Yasu...there is no shot. And this isn’t a doctor’s office. This is your bedroom. You live here. With me.
: It is?...
: But I was just somewhere else a second ago. How did I get here so quickly?
: Yasu...why were you taking off your clothes?...
: So the doctor can take pictures of me.
: Pictures?...
: For his notes.
: He takes one of the front...and then one of the back...and then gives me a shot so I can go home.
: He does what?...
: Did I mess something up?...
: I haven’t been to the examination room in a long time, so I might have made a mistake.
: Touka...you’re crying...
: What happened?...
: Nothing...
: Nothing happened, Yasu.
: I’m fine.
: *Sniff* Now, please make yourself look at least somewhat presentable as we’ll be heading to the manor for the rest of the night.
: The manor? How come?
: You needn’t worry about that. Just put your clothes back on and I’ll make a call to my driver.
: Okay! Thank you for always being kind enough to let a pathetic bug like me into your beautiful home!
: Of course...
: Don’t mention it.
: Hello?
: How much can I trust you?
: An adequate amount.
: It needs to be more than that.
: Why? What’s going on? Did something else happen with Yasu after I left?
: Yes. But it’s not something I want to talk about over the phone.
: Then where does trust come into this?
: In the form of you treating her the way she is meant to be treated and not like some piece of meat who exists to arouse you.
: Are you suggesting that I haven’t been doing that?
: No.
: But that doesn’t mean someone else hasn’t.
: And I’ll be damned if I let it happen again.
Touka hangs up the phone...
And my already complicated relationship with Yasu seems to get even worse.
No one’s affection goes anywhere-
And you fall asleep in the wrong direction.
